outcome: Let an output contract declare value checks and hold the export to them (issue 17, item 3): declare_output accepts not-null and inclusive range checks on the columns the contract names, export_result verifies them against the dataset before anything is written and refuses a violation with evidence, and transform advice counts them the way export does before saying a result matches the contract
criteria: declare_output accepts checks as a list ({"column", "not_null", "min", "max"}), as an object keyed by column, or inline in a column declaration; bounds are numbers, or ISO dates or timestamps; a check on a name the contract does not use, a check with nothing to check, a bound of another kind, min above max, a range on a column declared string or boolean, or two checks on one column are refused with advice naming the accepted shape; the contract summary, get_output_contract and the declaration sentence show the checks, and changing them on an open contract is an amendment that needs a reason

export_result refuses a dataset whose checked column holds a null under not_null, or a non-null value outside [min, max], with a recoverable CONTRACT_MISMATCH whose problems carry evidence (the declared check, the counts of null and out-of-range values, the observed minimum and maximum, and up to five offending rows of the columns the contract names) and no repair transform, before any file is written; a range on a column that is neither numeric nor temporal, or a bound whose kind does not fit the column, is a mismatch too; a passing export records each check with its counts in the contract evidence and the audit event

Null and unknown behavior is defined and holds: a null value passes a range check and fails not_null, a NaN is outside every range, and an empty dataset passes value checks (rows states whether it may be empty); a transform result is said to match the contract (matches_contract) only after its checks are counted as export counts them, and a result whose shape matches but whose values fail is named in contract_checks_failed advice with the counts

A contract that declares no checks behaves exactly as before, the backend reads no task and invents no value, a new MADR records the decision, README.md and the declare_output and export_result tool descriptions describe checks, and tests under tests/ with positive and negative examples on fixtures unrelated to DataSpace cover each case above; the backend test suite passes

reason: Bind the decision record this work wrote for value checks, MADR 0020, as criterion 4 names it

note: ContractCheck is stored with the contract (checks_json, migrated for older workspaces). parse_contract reads checks from the checks argument, an object keyed by column, or keys inside a column declaration. bind_checks maps them to dataset columns through match_columns, and DuckDBEngine.check_values counts nulls and out-of-range values with bound parameters in one scan, plus a bounded sample of offending rows. Export evidence names the observed extremes observed_min and observed_max so they cannot be confused with the declared bounds. The executor counts the same checks over previews, materializations and raw_query results for advise_contract, which says matches_contract only after counting and otherwise gives contract_checks_failed. declaration_checks teaches refused declarations. MADR 0020 was written in this outcome and bound by amendment. tests/test_contract_checks.py has 27 tests; the backend suite passes (474). The 8 media tests still fail on the local FFmpeg, unrelated to this change.
